en-US.description: Spec-first continuity framework for AI-assisted development
en-US.longDescription: Anchors ties spec, feature and test together through a shared identity code, then confronts each artifact against the rules declared in anchors.yaml. It maps the project as a graph, propagates change from the anchor outward, and gates every step — so work guided by AI stays anchored to what was decided.
en-US.name: Anchors
en-US.releaseNotes:
New: aliases: — short names for the paths of anchors.yaml
A path written in anchors.yaml is often long, and the same prefix repeats across layers, guides,
derived templates and gate exceptions. aliases: names it once:
aliases:
  "@app": apps/mobile/src
  "@guides": docs/engineering/guides
layers:
  ui:
    pattern: "@app/screens/**/*.tsx"
    kind: code
governs:
  - from: "@guides/SCREEN_GUIDE.md"
    governs: ui
An alias is named @ and a word and stands for a path relative to the root. It is translated as
the first segment of a path, in every field that holds one: layers, guides, derived,
frozen_paths, suites and their reports, docs, changelog, pipeline.workflows, gate
exceptions, dialect globs. The translation happens once, when the configuration loads; every
command reads the translated path.
A path that cites an alias aliases: does not declare refuses the configuration, naming the
field; a real folder named with @ (@scope/pkg) is kept as written. An alias that opens with
another, or names no path, is refused too.
Everything in the v0.1.351 notes still applies: run anchors migrate once, crossing format 8.
